Class AlgoReplayCalendar

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.service.AlgoReplayCalendar
@Service public class AlgoReplayCalendar extends Object
The trading calendar as a decision engine sees it: which days a run visits at all, which day an instrument last had a close on, and which day an order decided today can actually be filled on.

The three questions are separate on purpose. A run walks the application wide trading calendar, because a portfolio has to be valued on every day the application considers a trading day. An instrument, however, follows the calendar of its own exchange, and a crypto currency follows none at all - so a day the run visits may still be a day on which a particular instrument neither has a price nor can be traded.

The instrument side of this used to live privately in AlgoMeanReversionEvaluationService. It is shared here because a historical replay has to answer exactly the same question for a past day that the live evaluation answers for yesterday, and two implementations of a trading calendar would eventually disagree.

    • runDates

      public List<LocalDate> runDates(LocalDate openingDate, LocalDate endDate)
      The days a run evaluates, which are the application wide trading days after the opening date up to and including the end date. The opening date itself is excluded: its closing state is the immutable starting point of the environment and no decision may be taken on it.
      Parameters:
      openingDate - the immutable opening date of the simulation environment
      endDate - the last day to evaluate, which the caller has already checked to be in the past
      Returns:
      the ordered days to evaluate, empty when the range contains no trading day

    • completedDate

      public LocalDate completedDate(Security security, LocalDate through)
      The last day up to through on which the instrument had a session, which is the day its closing price and therefore a decision about it belongs to.
      Parameters:
      security - the instrument
      through - the day the caller wants a completed close for, inclusive
      Returns:
      that day, which is through itself whenever the instrument traded on it
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - MEAN_REVERSION_CALENDAR_REQUIRED when the instrument has no exchange to read a calendar from, or its exchange has been closed for longer than a month; MEAN_REVERSION_INACTIVE_INSTRUMENT when the resulting day lies outside the instrument's active period

    • nextEligibleClose

      public Optional<LocalDate> nextEligibleClose(Security security, LocalDate decisionDate, LocalDate horizonEnd)
      The day an order decided at the close of decisionDate is filled on: the first session of the instrument strictly after that day, still inside the run.

      A decision is never executed at the price it was taken on. A run that ends before the instrument trades again leaves the order unfilled, which is why this returns an empty result rather than a date beyond the horizon.

      Parameters:
      security - the instrument to be traded
      decisionDate - the closing day the decision was taken on
      horizonEnd - the last day of the run
      Returns:
      the fill day, or empty when the instrument has no further session within the run

      directBond - captured direct-bond flag, or null to read the entity
